refnamediv.refpurpose: API for temporarily muting noisy output to the main kernel console

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: io.systemd.MuteConsole is a small helper interface used to temporarily suppress kernel and PID 1 messages on the system console, for example while a display manager or desktop session is running, so that log output does not corrupt the graphical login screen. It is served by systemd-mute-console1 on the /run/systemd/io.systemd.MuteConsole socket, and can be introspected and called with varlinkctl1.

refsect1.title: Security
refsect1.para: Muting is system-wide: it suppresses the kernel console log level and PID 1 status output on the main console, not merely the caller's view of it. The socket (/run/systemd/io.systemd.MuteConsole) is root-owned with SocketMode=0644, so only the superuser and members of appropriate groups may invoke it. No polkit interaction takes place.

refsect1.title: Interface Definition
refsect1.para: The following interface definition is exposed:
refsect1.programlisting:
# API for temporarily muting noisy output to the main kernel console interface io.systemd.MuteConsole
# Mute kernel and PID 1 output to the main kernel console # [Requires 'more' flag] method Mute( # Whether to mute the kernel's output to the console (defaults to true). kernel: ?bool, # Whether to mute PID1's output to the console (defaults to true). pid1: ?bool ) -> ()

example.title: Mute kernel and PID 1 console output
example.para: The call uses the more flag (see Mute() below), hence --more.

refsect1.title: History
refsect1.para: The io.systemd.MuteConsole interface was added in version 259.
